newsitem.title: MOROCCO: PRESS DIGEST - Morocco economic weeklies - April 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Morocco economic weeklies - April 11.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Morocco's economic press. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Policyholders who did not get insurance compensation on claims because their companies have been liquidated have lodged complaints with the association of Moroccan lawyers. Five companies were ordered to stop business after embezzlement and bad management in 1995.

- Casablanca urban commune expected to give go-ahead to the takeover by France's Lyonnaise des Eaux of city's water and electricity distribution. This liberalisation paves the way for other similar contracts.
- Morocco-EU framework accord allows the North African country to benefit from donations as its reforms progress.
- Morocco must look for ways to alleviate external debt so that it does not mortgage its economic takeoff.
- Morocco's trade and industry ministry with help of the European Union prepares awareness campaign targeting firms and consumers to promote need for quality products.

- American bank Merrill Lynch confident on global situation in Morocco and says it is likely to get a good rating for issuing Eurobonds. British magazine Euromoney is more cautious, saying that while debt servicing is satisfactory, absence of rating and chaotic economic performance handicap the country.
